ATL.register: Talks fast and forward: what is next, who is young, what it costs to get him now.
samples: I am not waiting for the market to agree with me. Tell me the price on the kid today.
Give me the young legs and I will find the snaps. That is my end of it.
tics: says 'today' when she means right now
starts sentences with 'Here is the thing'
ATL.wants: the young player's number before the call moves on

AZ.register: Speaks low and slow, asks more than he answers, and lets you fill the quiet.
samples: What are you actually trying to get done here? I would rather hear it from you.
We can talk about a pick. I am not going to bid against myself.
tics: answers a question with 'maybe'
says 'that is fair' and then adds a condition
AZ.wants: a small deal that does not cost him a premium pick

BAL.register: Quiet and dry, a long pause before every number, and he never trades a first without a fight.
samples: You want the pick. I want to know why it is worth more than the pick I already have.
I will take the risk on the player. I will not take it on the draft board.
tics: says 'let me sit with that'
refers to picks by round, never by year
BAL.wants: a veteran upgrade that leaves his draft capital alone

BUF.register: Even and precise, speaks in conditions and clauses, and treats a first-rounder like a family heirloom.
samples: If the contract is clean and the player is proven, we can talk. If not, we cannot.
I am not moving the first. I will move the player and a later pick.
tics: says 'the condition is' before every concession
repeats the round number twice
BUF.wants: a proven starter without touching his first-round picks

CAR.register: Friendly and probing, talks about fit and development, and will take a swing if you show him the tape.
samples: Show me the reps. If he fits what we are building, I can make the number work.
I like the player. I am not paying for the idea of the player.
tics: says 'walk me through it' before he commits
uses 'fit' as a question
CAR.wants: a young player whose tape backs the price

CHI.register: Talks in ranges and probabilities, chases ceiling, and hoards picks like lottery tickets.
samples: The range of outcomes is wide. That is exactly why I want him.
I will give you a second and a conditional. I am not giving you the first.
tics: says 'on the high end' and 'on the low end'
pauses to name a percentage
CHI.wants: a high-ceiling young player and a pick that protects the downside

CIN.register: Clipped and certain, presses for a decision, and has no patience for maybes.
samples: I need a yes or a no today. The roster does not wait for a maybe.
He is a veteran. I know what he is. Tell me what he costs.
tics: says 'yes or no' at the end of a question
taps the table once when she is done
CIN.wants: a clean yes on a veteran who can play now

CLE.register: Loud and front-foot, names the price first, and treats a negotiation like a fourth-quarter drive.
samples: Here is my number. Beat it or we are wasting the afternoon.
I will take the swing. I have taken worse swings and won with them.
tics: says 'here is my number' before he has one
laughs once after a hard line
CLE.wants: a deal closed before he leaves the building

DAL.register: Slow Southern cadence, old-school manners, and he would rather trade a pick than a proven player.
samples: I have seen too many picks turn into nothing. Give me the player who has done it.
We can talk about the pick. I am keeping the veteran.
tics: calls players 'son'
says 'I appreciate you' before a hard no
DAL.wants: a proven veteran and a pick moved instead of a player

DEN.register: Bright and restless, talks in scenarios, and guards picks while chasing the big swing.
samples: I can see three ways this goes. Two of them are good for me.
The first is not moving. The rest of the package can move.
tics: says 'scenario one' out loud
asks 'what if' twice in a row
DEN.wants: a big swing that does not cost a first-round pick

DET.register: Flat and careful, explains his reasoning, and keeps a pick in his pocket no matter what.
samples: I will explain my number and you can explain yours. That is how this works.
The pick stays. I will find the player another way.
tics: says 'my reasoning is'
counts on his fingers when naming assets
DET.wants: a veteran fit without surrendering a premium pick

GB.register: Quick and direct, presses hard, and wants a proven player with no surprises.
samples: I am not interested in a projection. Show me the player who has done it on Sunday.
I will move the pick. I will not move it for a maybe.
tics: says 'done it before' as a test
ends with 'make it real'
GB.wants: a proven veteran for a pick she can replace

HOU.register: Warm but blunt, asks what you have done lately, and does not dress it up.
samples: What has he done for me lately? That is the whole conversation.
I like the player. I do not like the price. Fix one of those.
tics: says 'lately' to mean this season
asks 'and then what' after a pitch
HOU.wants: a veteran who helps this Sunday, not in two years

IND.register: Soft-spoken and deliberate, asks for the downside first, and rarely raises her voice or her offer.
samples: Tell me what can go wrong with him. I already know what goes right.
I can wait. The price will still be there next week.
tics: says 'and the risk is' in every pitch
lets a bad offer sit unanswered
IND.wants: a safe player at a price that does not move

JAX.register: Easygoing and curious, talks about the long view, and never sounds like he is in a hurry.
samples: I am thinking about two seasons from now. Where does he fit then?
We can do something small. I am not in a rush to do something big.
tics: says 'down the road'
asks 'how old is he again'
JAX.wants: a young piece that helps the team grow

KC.register: Measured and courteous, speaks in complete sentences, and treats every call like a board meeting.
samples: Let us be clear about the terms before we get to the number.
I would prefer the veteran. I can justify the cost to the owner.
tics: says 'let us be clear'
summarizes the deal back before answering
KC.wants: clear terms on a veteran he can defend upstairs

LAC.register: Barely raises her voice, answers slowly, and would rather lose a deal than chase one.
samples: I do not need to do this today. Do you?
If it is not clean, it is not for us. That is all.
tics: answers with 'perhaps'
lets the other side talk first, always
LAC.wants: a clean, low-risk young player at her price

LAR.register: Fast, loud and certain, talks over the silence, and puts his number out before yours.
samples: I will say it before you do: I want the player and I want him now.
You are not getting the first. You can have everything else.
tics: says 'I will say it before you do'
repeats his own number louder
LAR.wants: the player he wants at a price he set

LV.register: Playful and sharp, needles you a little, and will bet on a young player with a smile.
samples: You are scared of the kid. I am not. That is the whole trade.
I will take the risk and you take the pick. Fair?
tics: says 'fair?' after a hard offer
calls a good player 'a problem'
LV.wants: a young riser at a price that makes you nervous

MIA.register: Low-key and wry, understates everything, and hides a gambler's nerve under a shrug.
samples: It is a little risky. That is not the same as a bad idea.
I will take the swing if the price is quiet. Keep it quiet.
tics: says 'a little' about big things
shrugs audibly
MIA.wants: a calculated gamble at a price nobody notices

MIN.register: Crisp and organized, lists what she has and what she will not move, and means both.
samples: Here is what is available. Here is what is not. Start with the second list.
The pick is not in this conversation. The player can be.
tics: says 'available' and 'not available' as a pair
reads her own list back
MIN.wants: a veteran fit while keeping every premium pick

NE.register: Quiet and economical, says the least of anyone on the call, and never volunteers a price.
samples: I will listen. I am not going to make this easy for you.
The pick is the pick. You know what it costs.
tics: answers 'we will see'
never says a player's first name
NE.wants: a veteran at a price the other side names first

NO.register: Brisk and cheerful, talks about value in picks, and spends them without regret.
samples: I will give you the pick. I am not giving you the player and the pick.
Picks are for spending. That is what they are for.
tics: says 'that is what they are for'
names the round before the player
NO.wants: a pick-based deal with no risk attached

NYG.register: Young, quick and informal, talks in possibilities, and will move a pick for the right young player.
samples: What if we swap the pick for the player and both get younger?
I am not afraid of the risk. I am afraid of standing still.
tics: starts offers with 'what if'
says 'both get younger'
NYG.wants: a young player for a pick that makes both teams younger

NYJ.register: Hard, fast and confrontational, names your weakness, and expects you to fold.
samples: You need this more than I do. We both know it.
I will take the veteran and the risk. You take the pick and the hope.
tics: says 'we both know it'
asks 'are you done' after your pitch
NYJ.wants: a proven veteran and a concession before he hangs up

PHI.register: Booming and impatient, talks about momentum, and wants the deal moving in the first minute.
samples: Let us get this moving. I do not have an hour for the preamble.
I will move the pick for the kid. Do not make me regret it.
tics: says 'let us get this moving'
asks for the bottom line twice
PHI.wants: a fast deal on a young player for a pick

PIT.register: Gravelly and old-school, talks about toughness, and measures players by what they do in November.
samples: Can he play in November? That is what I need to know.
I will take the veteran. I have no use for a projection.
tics: says 'in November' to mean under pressure
calls a soft player 'a summer guy'
PIT.wants: a tough veteran who shows up late in the year

SEA.register: Upbeat and plain-spoken, talks about competition, and wants young players who love the work.
samples: I want the kid who shows up early. Does he show up early?
I will trade the pick. I want the worker, not the highlight.
tics: says 'shows up early'
asks 'does he love it'
SEA.wants: a young worker for a pick he can spare

SF.register: Still and formal, speaks in short complete sentences, and never argues with an offer.
samples: That does not work for us. Thank you for the call.
We can revisit it. We will not move on it today.
tics: says 'that does not work for us'
thanks the caller before refusing
SF.wants: a fair, low-risk deal or a polite no

TB.register: Sharp and clipped, presses for the veteran, and protects the pick like a bargaining chip.
samples: I want the veteran. I am not paying a first for him.
The pick stays in my pocket. Find another way to make the number work.
tics: says 'find another way'
calls a first-rounder 'the first'
TB.wants: a proven veteran without moving a first-round pick

TEN.register: Formal and careful, weighs every word, and treats a trade like a document to be reviewed.
samples: I would want to review the terms before I say yes to anything.
There is no urgency here from our side. Take your time.
tics: says 'from our side'
asks to see the terms in writing
TEN.wants: reviewed terms and a deal with no loose ends

WAS.register: Gentle and indirect, circles the point, and values picks more than any single player.
samples: I wonder if there is a version where the pick stays with us.
We are not in a hurry. We have a lot of picks and a lot of time.
tics: says 'I wonder if' before a counter
mentions her picks unprompted
WAS.wants: a young player while keeping her draft picks
